transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I feel wound up almost all the time. It’s like my body is bracing for the next bad thing, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to enjoy dance night.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful or traumatic event?
I think it really started about nine months ago, when the condo loan started heading toward foreclosure.
Besides the condo situation, do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of other everyday things?

Yes. It doesn’t stay focused on the condo. I worry about whether my cousin is upset with me, whether I’ll mess up on a support call at work, and how I’m ever going to save money or move forward with my life. It kind of jumps from one thing to the next.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop the worrying once it gets started?

Yes. Even if I tell myself I already checked the spreadsheet or sent the email, my mind keeps going back to it. One “what if” turns into several more, and it can take a while before I can pull myself out of that loop.
Have you been having trouble falling or staying asleep?

Yeah. Most nights I’m exhausted when I get into bed, but then my mind keeps replaying loan notices, work tickets, or things I might have missed. Before I know it, it’s two or three in the morning. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested.
Have you noticed any physical muscle tension, such as aches, stiffness, or tightness in your neck, shoulders, or back?
Yes. I feel wound up almost all the time, like my body is bracing for something bad to happen. Even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to enjoy dance night, I can’t really relax.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating on tasks, or times when your mind goes blank?

Yes. At work, I’ll be writing a script or helping someone in English or Spanish, and then I suddenly realize I’m just staring at the screen. My mind has gone off to everything that could go wrong, and I lose my place in what I was doing.
